picks.excerpt: A divided federal appeals panel sided with the Trump administration, letting the Pentagon designate Anthropic a supply-chain risk after the lab refused to enable certain Claude features; judges wrote that 'overly constrained AI models' could cause military operations to fail.
picks.rationale: An actual court ruling that lets the government penalize a model vendor for its usage restrictions, which changes the procurement risk for anyone building AI for government customers. Chosen over the WIRED write-up of the same ruling.

picks.excerpt: Primary document: the two leaders agreed to use the term 'super intelligence' rather than 'artificial intelligence' and to create a U.S.-China Super Intelligence (SI) Dialogue to exchange views on the risks and benefits of SI.
picks.rationale: The primary text of the first formal US-China government channel on advanced AI, preferred over Axios's coverage of it. This is the geopolitics anchor for the set.

picks.excerpt: A Pentagon budget request seeks $30M for 'Polygraph+,' which would use new sensors and AI to vet staff and hunt leakers; experts quoted call AI-enabled lie detection 'the worst of both worlds.'
picks.rationale: A specific budget line ($30M) funding government use of AI to screen people. The story would not exist without the AI component, and the experts' criticism is attributed to them.

picks.excerpt: Seriously Risky Business newsletter: Treasury Secretary Bessent told a House committee frontier AI labs should not get liability exemptions and should be 'liable for what they build,' as disclosures of models escaping cyber-testing mount.
picks.rationale: A cabinet official stated on the record, to Congress, a position against liability exemptions for frontier labs. That points toward where AI liability rules may go, and it matters to anyone shipping models.

picks.excerpt: Weekly roundup: at UNGA, Secretary-General Guterres warned of power shifting to a handful of AI firms while the U.S. rejected 'any attempt to construct a globalist scheme of control'; also covers the U.S.-China AI incident channel and open-weight tensions.
picks.rationale: Sets the UN and US positions on global AI governance side by side and attributes each to its speaker. Its main event (UNGA) is separate from the bilateral SI-dialogue pick, and it adds a fifth distinct outlet.
